definition: AutoML Evaluation and Benchmarking compares automated systems under controlled datasets, tasks, metrics, budgets, and repetitions. A valid benchmark separates algorithm quality from search effort and reports variation rather than relying on one lucky run.
intuition: A benchmark is an experiment about AutoML systems: hold the comparison protocol fixed, vary the system, and measure quality and cost across more than one task.
advantages: Separates predictive quality from runtime, budget, and variance.
Supports reproducible comparison across datasets and tasks.
limitations: Different time limits, hardware, seeds, and tuning rules can invalidate direct comparisons.
One benchmark suite cannot represent every dataset, task, or deployment constraint.
